slot.brief: Sum to n terms of a series whose general term splits as f(k) − f(k+1) (e.g. 1/(k(k+2))); ask for the sum in closed form.

stem: The sum of the first $n$ terms of $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{k(k+2)}$ is
working:
$\dfrac{1}{k(k+2)}=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac1k-\dfrac1{k+2}\right)$; $S_n=\dfrac12\left(1+\dfrac12-\dfrac1{n+1}-\dfrac1{n+2}\right)=\dfrac{n(3n+5)}{4(n+1)(n+2)}$.

Independent check: Use \(\frac1{k(k+2)}=\frac12(\frac1k-\frac1{k+2})\). The sum telescopes to \(\frac{n(3n+5)}{4(n+1)(n+2)}\).
solution:
Using partial fractions, $\frac{1}{k(k+2)}=\frac12\bigl(\frac1k-\frac1{k+2}\bigr)$, so the sum telescopes:
$$S_n=\frac12\biggl(1+\frac12-\frac1{n+1}-\frac1{n+2}\biggr)=\frac{n(3n+5)}{4(n+1)(n+2)}.$$
